# Visual review

Producer self-review of the local Crossing Law demo. Not owner approval or independent review.

Reviewed `.design-dna/check/review-1-home.png`, the native wide/narrow first screens, all four sources' contact sheets, the unobstructed Hafnia expertise and people inner captures, and live browser behavior.

- herzog: reference shows an oversized sans/serif name beneath a left text block and right navigation, a sculptural metal plate, and pale service layers moving through a held region; build shows the same opening relationship, a scooter metal plate, and slower-moving pale layers over a dark final panel; difference: shorter English copy, fewer practice areas, dark reading text for contrast, and the generated scooter subject. The memorable layered encounter comes through, with normal-flow mobile content.
- hafnia: reference shows large off-center photography with short adjacent copy and generous open ground; build shows a similarly off-center street illustration between a short heading and a small reading column; difference: the family's crossing replaces staff photography, and typography stays with the dominant source. The home recording includes a consent overlay, so the unobstructed studied inner captures and live source inspection were also consulted. No source video or cookie interface was copied.
- grace: reference shows 496px rounded panels in a horizontal strip with a plus control that reveals the longer copy within the panel; build shows the same clipped-next-panel invitation, independent plus/minus controls and local question/answer faces; difference: one question per panel, no testimonials, no embedded video, and the dominant source's dark-red/white palette. All three question toggles work.
- noah: reference shows a two-column lead and a narrower information rail, with simple links and a quiet dark conclusion; build shows a large closing statement, an adjacent navigation rail, and plain-language demo/privacy information below; difference: fewer content entries and no invented career facts or contact identity. The information hierarchy remains recognizable without reproducing the source's portrait.

## Functional review

- Mobile menu opens, follows Questions, and closes; Escape closes and returns focus to its trigger.
- Question panels expose their answers and update aria-expanded; the consultation answer explicitly states that no legal services are offered.
- At 320 CSS pixels the document stays within the viewport; intentionally horizontal question cards remain inside their own scroll strip.
- Reduced motion removes the held stage and image transform, restoring normal reading flow.
- No intake, remote scripts, analytics, production contact endpoint, or deployment. All page links are local anchors.
- All reading colors use measured reference values. Coral on white measured 2.985:1 and was replaced by the source's dark reading ink, except for the identity wordmark.

## Unresolved

- The installed source registry still marks Minimal Gallery inactive against obsolete minimalgallery.com, although its canonical minimal.gallery directory and these three exact editorial entries are reachable and were inspected in this run. The build cannot clear the current source-eligibility check while that shared registry remains unchanged.
- Hafnia's automated home video retains the consent overlay, and Grace's vertical recording does not traverse its horizontal strip. Their unobstructed inner images and live interaction observations supplement those limits; they do not turn the recordings into complete interaction audits.
